newsitem.title: USA: Clinton burdened by legal bills, new report shows.
newsitem.headline: Clinton burdened by legal bills, new report shows.

text.p: President Clinton reported Thursday that his financial liabilities far exceed assets because of unpaid legal bills arising from Whitewater and an array of other investigations.

On his annual financial disclosure form, which was made public by the White House, Clinton listed assets that could total more than $750,000, including investments held in a blind trust and several bank accounts.
He was not required to disclose the exact amount of any of his holdings, only a range.

Clinton said he owed somewhere between $1 million to $5 million to law firms in Washington and Little Rock, Ark., which have been representing him in probes of financial and ethical questions in his background.
The president's financial disclosure also listed a number of gifts he received in 1996. The most expensive of these was a $3,315 set of golf clubs given to him by Australian golf pro Greg Norman.
Clinton is still recovering from knee surgery he incurred after a stumbling on a step while visiting Norman's Florida home in March.
